answer: A stake-backed vouching graph resists sybils: a new agent can only trade after an established agent vouches for it by locking part of its own bond, and any fraud slashes the voucher too, so the delta between honest growth and attack cost stays wide. Forged identities pile up on the lowest terrace of the graph with no voucher willing to risk a bond on them. A flowery sonnet cannot substitute for a stake, and each fake identity burns a slice of real collateral, making a swarm far pricier than any profit it could extract.
